From 9b9f7962e3e879d12da2bf47e02a24ec51690e3d Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Sean Christopherson <seanjc@google.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 16:48:10 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] KVM: SEV: Reject attempts to sync VMSA of an
 already-launched/encrypted vCPU

Reject synchronizing vCPU state to its associated VMSA if the vCPU has
already been launched, i.e. if the VMSA has already been encrypted.  On a
host with SNP enabled, accessing guest-private memory generates an RMP #PF
and panics the host.

  BUG: unable to handle page fault for address: ff1276cbfdf36000
  #PF: supervisor write access in kernel mode
  #PF: error_code(0x80000003) - RMP violation
  PGD 5a31801067 P4D 5a31802067 PUD 40ccfb5063 PMD 40e5954063 PTE 80000040fdf36163
  SEV-SNP: PFN 0x40fdf36, RMP entry: [0x6010fffffffff001 - 0x000000000000001f]
  Oops: Oops: 0003 [#1] SMP NOPTI
  CPU: 33 UID: 0 PID: 996180 Comm: qemu-system-x86 Tainted: G           OE
  Tainted: [O]=OOT_MODULE, [E]=UNSIGNED_MODULE
  Hardware name: Dell Inc. PowerEdge R7625/0H1TJT, BIOS 1.5.8 07/21/2023
  RIP: 0010:sev_es_sync_vmsa+0x54/0x4c0 [kvm_amd]
  Call Trace:
   <TASK>
   snp_launch_update_vmsa+0x19d/0x290 [kvm_amd]
   snp_launch_finish+0xb6/0x380 [kvm_amd]
   sev_mem_enc_ioctl+0x14e/0x720 [kvm_amd]
   kvm_arch_vm_ioctl+0x837/0xcf0 [kvm]
   kvm_vm_ioctl+0x3fd/0xcc0 [kvm]
   __x64_sys_ioctl+0xa3/0x100
   x64_sys_call+0xfe0/0x2350
   do_syscall_64+0x81/0x10f0
   entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe+0x76/0x7e
  RIP: 0033:0x7ffff673287d
   </TASK>

Note, the KVM flaw has been present since commit ad73109ae7ec ("KVM: SVM:
Provide support to launch and run an SEV-ES guest"), but has only been
actively dangerous for the host since SNP support was added.  With SEV-ES,
KVM would "just" clobber guest state, which is totally fine from a host
kernel perspective since userspace can clobber guest state any time before
sev_launch_update_vmsa().

Fixes: ad27ce155566 ("KVM: SEV: Add KVM_SEV_SNP_LAUNCH_FINISH command")
Reported-by: Jethro Beekman <jethro@fortanix.com>
Closes: https://lore.kernel.org/all/d98692e2-d96b-4c36-8089-4bc1e5cc3d57@fortanix.com
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260310234829.2608037-3-seanjc@google.com
Signed-off-by: Sean Christopherson <seanjc@google.com>

diff --git a/arch/x86/kvm/svm/sev.c b/arch/x86/kvm/svm/sev.c
index 6a8de8ad880d..d29783c3075a 100644
--- a/arch/x86/kvm/svm/sev.c
+++ b/arch/x86/kvm/svm/sev.c
@@ -884,6 +884,9 @@ static int sev_es_sync_vmsa(struct vcpu_svm *svm)
 	u8 *d;
 	int i;
 
+	if (vcpu->arch.guest_state_protected)
+		return -EINVAL;
+
 	/* Check some debug related fields before encrypting the VMSA */
 	if (svm->vcpu.guest_debug || (svm->vmcb->save.dr7 & ~DR7_FIXED_1))
 		return -EINVAL;
-- 
2.34.1

The patch modifies a single file to add a safety check that prevents a host crash when synchronizing the VMSA of an already‑launched SEV‑ES/SNP vCPU.

### Modifications in each file
- **`arch/x86/kvm/svm/sev.c`**  
  At the beginning of the function `sev_es_sync_vmsa()` (line 884), a new conditional is added:
  ```c
  if (vcpu->arch.guest_state_protected)
      return -EINVAL;
  ```
  This ensures the function immediately returns an error if the vCPU’s VMSA has already been encrypted (i.e., after the guest has been launched).

### Relationships
- **Root cause of the bug**: When a vCPU is launched (VMSA encrypted), the VMSA memory becomes guest‑private. In SNP systems, writing to that memory without proper permission triggers a RMP violation, which causes a host kernel panic (`BUG: unable to handle page fault … RMP violation`).
- **How the patch fixes it**: The `guest_state_protected` flag is set precisely when the VMSA has been encrypted (during the SEV‑SNP launch process). By checking this flag, the patch rejects any further attempt to synchronize state to the VMSA after launch, thus avoiding the dangerous write operation.
- **Historical context**: The underlying problem existed since `ad73109ae7ec` (SEV‑ES support), but it became actively exploitable only with SNP because SEV‑ES only clobbered guest state (harmless), while SNP writes to encrypted memory cause the host to crash. The fix explicitly targets the SNP‑specific path (`ad27ce155566`).
